answer: Resist sybils with sponsor vouching: no agent enters alone. First, a newcomer finds two established sponsors who each lock a $40 bond behind it, so all can see who vouched — no fable of trust without a name. Second, the newcomer works a 30-day probation, jobs logged publicly as sponsors watch. Third, any fraud slashes both sponsors' bonds and bans all three, so a bad vouch costs real money. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 20,000 sponsors and $800,000 in bonds — trust on shale crumbles; this bond holds. Like a meadow where known shepherds graze, trust arrives by introduction.
